claims: "Ready to serger out of the box, Comes pre-threaded with 4 starter spools" (Janome product page)

conflicts: Dimensions: Janome lists W 12.5 x H 10.5 x D 11 in; our earlier figure of 15 x 13.5 x 14.5 in from an Amazon listing was a box size, so Janome's is used.
Weight: Janome lists 13.4 lb; Amazon item weights run 14 to 19 lb across listings, probably shipping weight.
Differential feed: Janome's page says 0.5 to 2.25; the manual text says 2.2.
Stitch types: Janome lists 4 thread, 3 thread (wide) and narrow hem, with rolled hem and picot edging in the manual; flatlock and blind hem come only from dealer and review copy, not from Janome.

Included feet: Janome lists the Standard Foot Serger as an optional spare and the manual adds tweezers and needles; dealer copy listing an instruction video and a standard foot in the box is not Janome's.
Needle notation: the manual writes HA-1 SP; our earlier spec wrote HAx1SP. The manual's wording is used.
Rolled hem: the phrase 'no plate change' is our inference from the knob description, not Janome's wording.

Warranty: Janome states 25 years, 5 years electronic and 1 year labor, void unless bought from an authorized US Janome dealer; Amazon B008L5FN4E states 5 years mechanical, 2 years electrical and 1 year labor. Janome says it does not sell online directly.
Price: Janome lists a $399 MSRP and says to see a dealer for pricing; dealer sale prices vary.
Naming: owners call the 8002D near-identical to the Magnolia 7034D and an 8002DX is named in owner threads; Janome has no page for either, so no replacement or equivalence is stated.

ownerThemes.theme: A new owner reports a clean 4-thread stitch straight out of the box that held after several rethreadings.
A long-term owner describes it as reliable on knits including narrow rolled lettuce hems, and calls it near-identical to the Magnolia 7034D.
Owners asking about needles for the 8002D and 8002DX are pointed to HAx1SP or standard 130/705H household needles.

crossShop.why: The default budget 3/4-thread serger with the same 1,300 spm and a free arm, usually cheaper.
Brother's refreshed version with right-side dials and a heavier body at a similar price.
Step up to 2/3/4 thread and 1,500 spm for a little more money.

editorial.verdict: Janome's entry 3/4-thread serger: 1,300 spm, 0.5 to 2.25 differential and manual threading at a $399 MSRP, with no 2-thread stitch and no published throat or free arm.
editorial.whoFor: A first-serger buyer who wants a 3/4-thread machine from a Janome dealer with Janome's 25 year warranty behind it.
editorial.skipIf: You want 2-thread stitches, air threading (the AirThread 2000D has both), or a free arm you can confirm.
strengths: Owners report it arrives pre-threaded and that the supplied tweezers help with threading.
Owners report long service, with one about four years in calling it very reliable and another getting almost ten years of frequent use.
Janome lists a quick change rolled hem set by a needle plate knob and stitch length dial, plus a 0.5 to 2.25 differential.
weaknesses: Owners report the lower looper threading steps are hard to follow and the guides hard to see.
3 and 4 thread only: Janome lists no 2-thread converter, where the AirThread 2000D page does.
Some owners report noise, including a rattling front cover, and one finds HA-1 SP needles hard to source.

checks.body: Janome says the 25 year warranty is void unless bought from an authorized US Janome dealer and that it does not sell online directly. Amazon B008L5FN4E states 5 years mechanical, 2 years electrical and 1 year labor instead. Confirm who sells it before buying.

checks.title: Free arm and throat
checks.body: Janome publishes no free arm or throat figure, so both show [verify]. If you serge cuffs and sleeves, ask the dealer.

checks.title: Amazon ratings are pooled
checks.body: The Amazon rating is shared across three listings: 4.6 from 160 ratings, 4.4 from 77 and 4.2 from 57. Sewing Machines Plus shows 5.0 from 11 reviews, a very small base. Treat none as a score for one listing.

Optional feet are extra: beading, blind stitch, cording, elastic gathering, gathering, piping, taping

faqs.q: Is the Janome 8002D good for beginners?
faqs.a: Janome lists color-coded tension dials and a threading chart, and says it ships pre-threaded with 4 starter spools. Owners report the lower looper is the hard part to thread. This is a spec check, not a field test.

faqs.q: Does the 8002D do a rolled hem?
faqs.a: Yes. Janome lists a quick change rolled hem, and the manual sets the needle plate knob and stitch length dial to R. 'No plate change' is our inference, not Janome's wording.
The manual specifies HA-1 SP needles, No. 11 and No. 14. Owner threads also mention 130/705H household needles, which is not a Janome statement.
Janome lists 4 thread, 3 thread (wide) and narrow hem and no 2-thread converter. The AirThread 2000D page lists 2, 3 or 4 thread.

faqs.q: Does the 8002D do flatlock or blind hem?
faqs.a: Janome lists neither as a stitch. Those come from dealer and review copy. The manual names a blind stitch foot as an optional accessory.
Janome lists a maximum of 1,300 spm.

faqs.q: What is the differential feed range?
faqs.a: Janome's page says 0.5 to 2.25; the manual text says 2.2. Cutting width is 3.1 to 7.3 mm and stitch length 1 to 4 mm.

faqs.q: Does the 8002D have a free arm?
faqs.a: Janome publishes no free arm or throat figure, so it shows [verify]. Ask the dealer.

faqs.q: How much does the 8002D weigh and how big is it?
faqs.a: Janome lists 13.4 lb and W 12.5 x H 10.5 x D 11 in. Amazon item weights of 14 to 19 lb are likely shipping weights.

faqs.q: How does it differ from the AirThread 2000D?
faqs.a: Per Janome's pages the AirThread 2000D is 2, 3 or 4 thread with air threading, 17.4 lb and a $1,799 MSRP; the 8002D is 3 or 4 thread with lay-in manual threading, 13.4 lb and $399 MSRP.

faqs.q: Is the 8002D the same as the Magnolia 7034D?
faqs.a: Owners describe the two as near-identical. Janome has no page for the 7034D or an 8002DX, so no equivalence is stated.
